metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to Thunderbird Account Settings, entered a 2-line plain text signature 'Anonym\nXYZ Lab', and closed settings to save.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Account Settings, locate Signature text field, type multi-line text, and close settings to persist.
metadata.task_rationale: Variation with a different academic name and institute; regex uses escaped dot to match literal period in 'Prof.'
metadata.explanation: Evaluator reads prefs.js after Thunderbird is closed and checks mail.identity.id1.htmlSigText contains the expected 2-line signature. Regex escapes the literal period in 'Prof.' to avoid wildcard matching.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches prefs.js from the VM via get_vm_file; the file is read after Thunderbird is closed (postconfig close_window + sleep), ensuring data is flushed to disk.
check_thunderbird_prefs parses Thunderbird's user_pref() format and checks mail.identity.id1.htmlSigText, which is the correct preference key for email signature text regardless of format mode.
The regex pattern 'Prof\. Kumar\nAI Research Institute' correctly escapes the literal period in 'Prof.' and uses \n for the required line break between the two signature lines.
The re.S (DOTALL) method is appropriate for pattern matching across the newline embedded in the signature string.

Implicit plain-text verification: when HTML mode is active, htmlSigText contains HTML markup (e.g.

...

,
), which would NOT match the plain-text regex — so passing the regex implicitly confirms plain-text format.
The metric returns 0 if result is None, providing safe failure on getter errors.
The type mismatch warning (get_vm_file returns Union vs str) is benign at runtime: single-file case returns cache_paths[0] which is Optional[str], and the metric handles None explicitly.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding an explicit unexpect rule checking mail.identity.id1.htmlSigFormat is not 'true', to directly verify the plain-text mode rather than relying on implicit regex filtering.
If multiple email identities could exist in the profile, verify that id1 corresponds to the correct account, or use a more dynamic identity lookup.
